single electron-induced upets in 28 nm and 45 nm CMOS bulk SRAMs were observed in the laboratory and that these upsets can have significant impact on space applications.
single electron upsets can occur in commercial SRAMs and that the cross sections for single electron upsets are strongly dependent on the SRAM bias and feature size.
Electron-induced upsets were observed in 28 nm and in 45 nm bulk SRAM cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
single-event effects in 28 and 45 nm SRAMs, and the electron contribution to the upset rate in space environments.
the impact of electron-induced single-event upsets on the reliability of current and future space missions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electrons are a serious threat for the reliability of current space electronics.
electron-induced upsets are an important contributor to upset rates in current and future technology nodes, and must be considered when assessing radiation effects on space systems.
electron-induced single event effects are an increasingly important consideration for the design, qualification and operation of space electronics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
single electron upsets in bulk SRAMs should be considered for future radiation effects experiments and simulations.
electron-induced upsets are a significant concern for current and future technology nodes, especially for the Jovians.

single electron upsets should not be ignored in the design of future space electronics, particularly in low power applications.
